external.description: TNB’s Project Chlorobloom is one of the most quietly interesting climate experiments in Malaysian industrial history. It deserves far more attention than it is getting. Somewhere in Manjung, Perak, flue gas from a coal-fired power plant is being fed into tanks of green water. Inside those tanks, microscopic algae are eating the carbon dioxide, multiplying at speed, and producing biomass that could one day end up in a fish farm, a fertiliser bag, or the fuel tank of a commercial aircraft. This is not science fiction. It is Project Chlorobloom — TNB’s Biological Carbon Capture and Utilisation initiative, which channels […]

external.description: By Norazam Nordin While public attention remains focused on rising living costs, tariffs and political developments, one strategic decision with the potential to shape Malaysia’s economy for decades has largely gone unnoticed. The launch of the Large Scale Solar 6 (LSS6) programme by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA) is far more than another renewable energy initiative. It signals Malaysia’s transition into a new phase of energy planning—from simply adding electricity generation capacity to building a smarter, more resilient energy system capable of supporting the country’s digital economy, high-tech industries and long-term decarbonisation goals.
